sources.articleTitle: Live: Beau Lamarre-Condon says phone and car tracing questions were for work
Beau Lamarre-Condon bought sim card under pseudonym a month before alleged murders, trial hears

headline: Former Officer Testifies In Sydney Double Murder Trial Proceedings
seoTitle: Lamarre-Condon Testimony In Sydney Murder Trial
metaDescription: A former police officer facing double murder charges testifies in a Sydney court regarding his use of a pseudonym and work-related tracking inquiries.
aiSummaryBullets: The defendant is currently undergoing cross-examination in a Sydney court regarding alleged double murder charges.
The former police officer stated he obtained a SIM card under a false name to report workplace bullying to the media.
Testimony also addressed the defendant's work-related questions concerning vehicle and phone tracking protocols.
aiContextParagraph: The ongoing trial involves a former police officer who stands accused of the murders of two men. During recent courtroom proceedings, the defendant has been subjected to nearly a week of cross-examination by the Crown. In his testimony, the former officer addressed his decision to purchase a SIM card using a pseudonym approximately one month prior to the alleged crimes. He claimed this action was motivated by a desire to communicate with media outlets regarding reports of bullying by a specific sergeant. Furthermore, the defense and prosecution have scrutinized the defendant's inquiries into technical matters such as vehicle and phone tracing procedures, which the former officer maintained were inquiries related to his official police duties. The trial continues as legal teams examine the evidence and the defendant’s explanations for his actions leading up to the events in question.
whyItIsViral: The case has maintained consistent local interest with coverage from multiple major Australian news organizations and ongoing judicial developments.
